archetypes.name: Distrustful low-trust skeptics
archetypes.text: People who see others as hard to trust and generally distrust institutions, yet are often politically engaged and check information online. Their wariness about people and institutions sits alongside a routine, stable private life and a fairly ordinary sense of financial security. They hold pessimistic views of the economy and democracy while still feeling personally content, and they tend to be cautious about technology and robots, but not overwhelmingly anxious about them.

archetypes.name: Distrustful satisfied routine skeptic
archetypes.text: People in this pattern distrust others and report being very satisfied with democracy while feeling uninterested in politics, a combination that suggests contentment with the system without engagement in it. Their personal finances feel improving yet they see their family income as below average and place themselves in the lower class, showing a gap between recent progress and perceived standing. They find life routine, happy but unexcited, and strongly favor traditional family roles, while sharply opposing technology and AI, which they regard with discomfort. They think science receives too much funding and taxes are too high, so their views on economics and innovation run against the usual pairing of optimism and trust.

archetypes.name: Distrustful, disengaged discontent
archetypes.text: People in this cluster combine deep distrust of institutions and other people with a sense of political alienation and financial strain, yet they are not hostile to technology or science. Their pessimism about the economy and democracy sits alongside a routine, mostly content personal life and steady family ties. Their views on machines and AI are mixed, sometimes uneasy but rarely alarmed, and they often feel the country spends too much on research or taxes.

archetypes.name: Distrustful but content high-earners
archetypes.text: People who report high personal happiness, above-average family income and a self-described middle or lower class, yet are dissatisfied with how democracy works and pessimistic about the economy. Their low trust in others and in institutions sits alongside strong comfort with technology and a sense that life is exciting. They are wary of AI and robots while still feeling financially secure, and they tend to combine a self-reliant, skeptical stance toward public institutions with a personal life centered on family and social contact.

archetypes.name: Distrustful tech-comfortable skeptics
archetypes.text: People who distrust others and nearly all institutions, yet feel strongly comfortable with robots and AI and see science spending as excessive. Their outlook pairs deep wariness of people and public bodies with enthusiasm for technology. They are dissatisfied with democracy and the economy, but personally content, financially stable, and fond of family time. Surprisingly, they reject the idea that technology is a threat while doubting the value of publicly funded research.
